correctness.rationale: For each long arc, an explicit allowed 2-path reduces it to shorter arcs; induction reduces every 1-cycle to the unit Hamiltonian cycle. The unit-edge cycle condition is rank one. The positive-residue displacement functional on all regular ordered pairs vanishes on every allowed elementary 2-path boundary and therefore on every Ω2-boundary, but evaluates to 2m+1 on the Hamiltonian cycle. This proves H1 is generated by one element of infinite order. The packaged verifier checks the defining identities for m through 12 and finite-field H1 for m through 5 over characteristics 2, 3, and 5.

value.rationale: The result covers an infinite canonical family of maximally dense strongly connected digraphs, identifies an exact integral generator, and gives a structural normal form plus an obstruction functional. It is not a parameter substitution or a finite census. The phenomenon is mathematically motivated because path homology is designed to detect directed connectivity, while dense random-digraph results can exhibit disappearance of first homology; the cyclic family instead retains a single robust class for every parameter.
